title: Embedding API latency: micro-batching strategy, kernel parameter tuning, and p99 tail analysis
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: reduce p99 latency for the Embeddings API under production traffic patterns while keeping cost-per-embedding neutral or improved. Scope: micro-batching/coalescing policy, kernel launch & parameter tuning (quantized vs fp16), and tail-latency analysis (cold-kernel, large-seq, and oversized batches). Out of scope for this ticket: model architecture changes and vector store client-side batching recommendations.

Background: internal dashboards show median latency ~18ms but p99 spikes between 180ms-420ms on small-batched requests during peak hours. Root causes suspected: (1) small request micro-batches missing coalescing window, (2) kernel launch overhead for certain quantized kernels, (3) interference from long-running KV-cache miss paths. This ticket will run controlled experiments, land runtime scheduler changes, and do a staged rollout with canary metrics.

Success metrics (measured on canary fleet and full rollout):
- p95 <= 60ms (stable)
- p99 <= 120ms on representative A/B traffic
- no >5% regression in embedding quality (cosine sim on seeded pairs)
- throughput >= current baseline at target cost envelope

Stakeholders: API infra, runtime team, product (Vector Search), SRE.
acceptance_criteria: p99 measured on production-like canary dataset is <= 120ms across 3 sustained 30m windows
Automated benchmark (bench/embeds/pipeline) shows <=5% token cost increase or improved cost per embedding
A/B quality check: embedding pairwise cosine correlation change < 0.02 on eval set (2000 pairs)
Rollout plan documented with rollback thresholds; SLO runbook updated
steps: 1) Reproduce p99 in controlled environment using continuous-replay of production request traces (w/ secrets scrubbed)
2) Baseline: capture current micro-batch coalescing latencies, kernel startup times, and GPU occupancy profiles (perfetto + nsys)
3) Implement adaptive coalescing: dynamic window that shortens on high concurrency and lengthens on low RPS (feature branch)
4) Kernel tuning: switch hot paths to optimized fused-kernels for common model shapes, adjust launch parameters for sm_80+ GPUs, compare quantized vs fp16 kernels
5) Add warm-up shim for first requests to mitigate cold-kernel overhead on newly spun workers
6) Run end-to-end benchmarks (p50/p95/p99) and embedding-quality regression tests
7) Canary rollout (10% traffic) with tight alerting: p99 increase > 10% triggers automated rollback
8) Full rollout with staged ramp and post-rollout review

notes: Trade-offs: longer coalescing windows reduce p99 but increase p50 for latency-sensitive single-request customers. Adaptive coalescing aims to get the best of both worlds by shortening windows under high RPS.
Risk: fused kernels may not be bitwise-identical; keep quality checks in CI and fast rollback hooks in the runtime
Mitigation: maintain per-node capability fingerprint (kernel-cap) and route incompatible nodes to safe path
